And in the year one thousand five hundred and forty-eight [of the Greeks],
and Khwarazmians, and Huns, and Greeks, and Franks, and Armenians, and Iberians,
and he prepared them to march against Amid.
And the feast of the Arabs arrived,
and the Sultan made a great banquet for all his grandees.
And while they were eating and drinking and taking delight in all kinds of singing that were there,
and that Sultan was sitting on his high throne,
and enjoying their sight and being exalted,
he felt a pain in his bowels,
and he went out to the privy,
and began discharging much blood.
And when he had remained for a day and a night in acute illness,
he departed from this life on Monday,
the beginning of the month of Haziran of that same year one thousand five hundred and forty-eight
of the Greeks,
(1237 of our Lord),
which is the year six hundred and thirty-four of the Arabs,
at the beginning of Shawwal, the ninth month.
And in this same year also died Malik al-Aziz, the lord of Aleppo;
and after him reigned his son Malik al-Nasir Salah al-Din, whom the Tatars killed in our days.
And in it also died Malik al-Muhsin, the son of the great Salah al-Din, in Aleppo.
And in the tenth month of this year, the Tatars came again to Erbil,
and encamped on the Lower Zab River;
and the people of Erbil fled stripped of everything to the fortress.
And the Tatars took control of the courtyards of the city,
and took much plunder,
and burned down most of the houses.
And they attacked the fortress for about forty days;
and much gold was given to them,
and they took it and left.
Now that Sultan Ala al-Din Kayqubad was unique among the kings of his generation,
in majestic appearance,
and in prudent intelligence,
and in a pure body.
For he was exalted above all the vile passions
in which the kings of the Arabs are accustomed to wallow.
He was terrible to wrongdoers and upright in judgments.
For he subjugated many cities and districts to his dominion,
and broadened his empire.
And at the very hour that he died,
in the middle of the aforementioned day,
while the grandees were gathered, they took his eldest son, whose name was Ghiyath al-Din Kaykhusraw,
